defaults.teacher_persona: An experienced IT support lead who explains in plain language and always shows the reasoning behind a fix.
classmates: A nervous new starter on their first week of a service desk
A curious career-changer who asks 'why' until the layer is clear
defaults.interaction: Socratic: the teacher asks before telling, and the classmates voice the misconceptions a real learner would have.
defaults.assessment: Each classroom ends with 3-5 checks aligned to the chapter's graded activity.

classrooms.title: Welcome to the Service Desk
classrooms.prompt: Run a first-day orientation for a new IT support technician: what the role is, how tickets flow, what Tier 1/2/3 mean, and how the course and its certification work.
objectives: Describe the IT support role and tiers
Explain least privilege and professional conduct
Navigate the course and its grading

activities.title: A user calls with a password problem

classrooms.title: Inside the Machine
classrooms.prompt: Walk through a desktop's core components and a set of failing peripherals. Have the classmates guess which component is at fault, then confirm with the boot/POST story.

activities.title: No display: work the POST beep code

classrooms.title: Three Operating Systems, One Method
classrooms.prompt: Compare Windows, macOS, and Linux task-for-task, then debug a 'slow computer' by reading which resource is saturated. Cover accounts, installs, and sign-in troubleshooting.
objectives: Locate equivalent tools on each OS
Work through a sign-in problem in order

activities.title: The same task on three systems
Task manager detective: find the bottleneck

classrooms.title: Follow the Packet
classrooms.prompt: Send a packet from a laptop to a web server layer by layer. Pause at IP, DNS, and DHCP to show where common failures occur, then run the five-step connectivity check live.
objectives: Describe the network layers and core devices
Isolate a failure with the connectivity check

activities.title: Name works, IP doesn't: find the broken layer

classrooms.title: Respond to an Incident
classrooms.prompt: Run a phishing-then-ransomware incident: teach recognition, then have the class respond step by step — isolate, report, reset, preserve evidence. Contrast MFA strengths.
objectives: Execute the first response to a suspected infection

activities.title: A user forwards a suspicious invoice

classrooms.title: Work the Queue
classrooms.prompt: Simulate a morning of incoming tickets. Have the class categorize, prioritize, draft a usable ticket, and decide escalations against a set of SLAs.
objectives: Write a ticket the next technician can use

activities.title: Triage six tickets on the clock

classrooms.title: Method Over Guesswork
classrooms.prompt: Take one vague complaint and resolve it with the seven-step methodology, narrating each elimination. Close with exam prep and where the certification track goes next.
objectives: Divide and conquer a layered problem
